drhp.business: We sell directly to independent jewellers and jewellery chains in India as well as select international markets. We supply our products to jewellery chains, including CaratLane Trading Private Limited, Kalyan Jewellers India Limited, Reliance Retail Limited, Malabar Gold & Diamonds FZCO, Tribhovandas Bhimji Zaveri Limited and Senco Gold Limited. With a workforce of over 400 employees, and integrated manufacturing capabilities, we offer end-to-end jewellery manufacturing solutions to our clients.

risks: We derived 53.19% of our revenue from our top ten customers for the period ended June 30, 2026, of which 33.36% of our revenue was derived from our top five customers.
Loss of such customers or reduction in business from such customers will have a significant adverse impact on our business and results of operation.
A substantial portion of our operating revenue is derived from a limited number of customers in the gems and jewellery industry.
In particular, our top five customers with whom we have long-term relationships accounted for 33.36% of our revenue from operations for the period ended June 30, 2026.
The table below sets forth the revenue derived from our top 10 customers, for the periods indicated:
There can be no assurance that we will continue to derive significant revenue from these customers.

The loss or reduction of sales to any of our key customers, whether due to the termination or non-renewal of contracts, inability to negotiate acceptable renewal terms, loss of market share of these customers, changes in product quality specifications, technological advancements, disputes, mergers or decline in their sales, reduced or delayed customer orders, store closures, labour strikes, or other work stoppages, could materially and adversely affect our business, operating results, financial condition, and cash flows.
Further, the volume and timing of sales to our top 10 clients may vary due to variations in demand for such customers’ products.

Further, our operations are subject to various export norms and customs regulations.

Any downturn in consumer demand, volatility in raw material prices (such as gold, diamonds, and platinum), changes in fashion trends, regulatory changes, increased competition, or any other adverse developments affecting the jewellery sector could significantly affect our revenues and profitability.

Changes in these regulations could increase our compliance costs, restrict our operational flexibility, or necessitate significant modifications to our manufacturing processes.
Although we strive to maintain compliance, we cannot assure that we will be able to adapt to new or evolving regulatory requirements in a timely or cost-effective manner.

We rely on the timely procurement of raw materials, including gold, diamonds, platinum, and precious or semi‑precious stones, to manufacture our jewellery products.
For further details on our raw material procurement practices, please refer to “Our Business – Our Manufacturing Process – Procurement of Raw Materials” on page 160.
Further, an increase in gold prices may also increase our operating costs including our procurement cost of raw materials which may adversely impact our profitability.

Relying on their adequate availability, we procure and source platinum and precious and semi-precious stones such as diamonds and gemstones from domestic vendors in the open market in India, on a spot basis and have not entered into long-term arrangements with our suppliers, since there are no restrictions on our purchases.
Accordingly, our business is affected by the availability, cost and quality of raw materials.
Further, we source our materials on a spot basis and do not enter into long-term contracts with our suppliers, making our business vulnerable to fluctuations in materials prices.

Prices of materials are influenced by factors beyond our control, including geopolitical conditions, production capacity constraints, transportation costs, infrastructure disruptions, regulatory changes, government policies, labour unrest, and competitive demand.

While we have not faced any supply chain disruptions in the three months ended June 30, 2026 and the last three Fiscals, any future disruption in the timely procurement of these materials from our existing vendors, or a failure to source suitable alternatives on acceptable terms, could adversely impact our production schedules, increase our costs, and materially affect our business and financial condition.

Further, the prices of our raw materials are also affected by fluctuations in global demand, supply chain disruptions and economic slowdowns, including on account of recent trade wars, increasing protectionist policies and the imposition of tariffs on goods originating from certain regions.
